title: No cabe duda de que: afirmar con seguridad

sections.content: No cabe duda de que (there is no doubt that) is a strong, formal way to assert a claim as settled fact -- and, unlike es cuestionable que, it takes the indicative, since it's affirming rather than evaluating uncertainty. It fits the historian's confident tone when the evidence for a claim is genuinely overwhelming. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: No cabe duda de que el ejemplo cubano y la lógica de la Guerra Fría empujaron a la política latinoamericana hacia una polarización cada vez más extrema.
items.english: There is no doubt that the Cuban example and Cold War logic pushed Latin American politics toward increasingly extreme polarization.

items.spanish: No cabe duda de que muchos militares latinoamericanos adoptaron lo que se conocería como la Doctrina de Seguridad Nacional.
items.english: There is no doubt that many Latin American militaries adopted what would become known as the National Security Doctrine.

items.spanish: No cabe duda de que esta polarización también radicalizó, en sentido contrario, a sectores de la izquierda latinoamericana.
items.english: There is no doubt that this polarization also radicalized, in the opposite direction, sectors of the Latin American left.

items.spanish: No cabe duda de que esta dinámica de polarización extrema resultaría extraordinariamente costosa para la región.
items.english: There is no doubt that this dynamic of extreme polarization would prove extraordinarily costly for the region.

sections.content: No cabe duda de que + indicative sits at the opposite end of the certainty scale from es cuestionable que + subjunctive, which you learned earlier -- the two phrases let a writer signal exactly how confident they are in a claim, just by choosing which one to use.
